signal: AirOps raised a $40M Series B led by Greylock and launched a suite of enterprise CMS and project-management integrations in March 2026 to manage and publish content at scale.

email.body1:
Cecile, saw AirOps raised the $40M Series B from Greylock and shipped a suite of enterprise CMS and project-management integrations this year.

Scaling that fast usually means more enterprise accounts in play across US and EMEA than reps can cover before they ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for AirOps off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Cecile, quick follow-up for AirOps.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can, especially across two regions. Most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need for the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings AirOps needs across your regions, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Cecile, last bit of proof for AirOps.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other Series-B AI startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Cecile, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority while you ramp post-raise across two regions, no problem at all. That stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a multi-region GTM motion? I will tailor it to AirOps either way.
